result.source_concept: bracelet made of beads on a cord

mappings.evidence: Each bead can have a letter, a number, or a little symbol painted on it.

mappings.source_element: number of beads on the cord
mappings.evidence: You can check how long the bracelet is by counting the beads (its length).

mappings.source_element: tying another beaded cord onto the end
mappings.evidence: If you want a bigger bracelet, you tie another beaded cord onto the end (concatenation).

mappings.source_element: removing a portion of beads from one spot to another
mappings.evidence: If you need just a small section, you carefully remove a portion of beads from one spot to another (substring).
The full bracelet is simply the entire sequence of these little beads.

result.process_summary: Both the bracelet and a string are linear sequences built from discrete units (beads or characters). Their length is measured by counting units, they can be extended by adding more units at the end, and a contiguous subset can be taken as a smaller sequence. The analogy maps the construction, measurement, extension, and extraction processes from the physical bracelet to the abstract string.
potential_breaks: Removing beads physically alters the original bracelet, whereas extracting a substring typically leaves the original string unchanged.
A bracelet has a tangible, flexible material and may involve knots when concatenating, which does not map perfectly onto the abstract, immutable nature of string concatenation.
